name: Perth
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Perth: resources company and tenement diligence, WA licensing rules, and support for WA proceedings.
hero_lede: Perth is the capital of Western Australia and the headquarters city for much of Australia's mining and energy industry. Investigative work connected to it concerns resources companies, junior explorers, tenements and offshore investors, and runs under Western Australian licensing and surveillance law as well as Commonwealth law.
intro: Perth is the capital of Western Australia and the base of Australia's resources sector. The City of Perth puts Greater Perth at about 2.38 million people, projected to reach 2.9 million by 2035, and Western Australia's gross state product at $458.8 billion in 2024-25. BHP, Rio Tinto, Fortescue, Hancock Prospecting, South32, Wesfarmers and Woodside Energy are headquartered in Perth, and Chevron, Shell, BP and INPEX have offices there. Mining, professional and technical services and finance lead the city's output, supported by mining equipment, technology and services firms. Western Australia accounts for about a third of ASX-listed companies, many of them mineral explorers, and Perth Airport is the country's western hub.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Perth because of its concentration of mining and energy companies, from global majors to hundreds of small listed explorers. Investors, offtakers and joint venture partners need to understand who controls a Perth company, the history of its directors and promoters, and whether its tenements and project claims hold up. Asian and other offshore investors in Western Australian critical minerals and energy projects want background on local partners. Litigants in the Supreme Court of Western Australia or the Federal Court need party and asset research. Western Australia's investigator licensing and surveillance laws determine how any fieldwork is done.

matters.title: Junior miner and promoter diligence
matters.text: Researching Perth-based explorers and their directors, major shareholders and promoters before investment or offtake, including prior companies, ASX queries and suspensions, ASIC actions, insolvencies and litigation, and patterns of capital raisings and related-party payments that a prospectus will not highlight.

matters.title: Tenement and project verification
matters.text: Checking that tenements claimed by a Western Australian company exist, are held by the stated entity, and are in good standing, and reviewing objections, plaints and joint venture arrangements alongside corporate records, so that project claims are tested before money is committed.

matters.title: Offshore investor partner reviews
matters.text: Supporting Asian, European and North American investors entering Western Australian critical minerals, lithium, iron ore or energy projects with background on local partners, their funding sources and connected entities, and their record in disputes with joint venturers, contractors and landholders.

matters.title: Contractor and supply chain integrity
matters.text: Assessing mining and oil and gas contractors, labour hire providers and suppliers based in Perth for ownership, phoenix activity indicators, safety and regulatory enforcement history, and links to client staff, where procurement on large remote projects creates opportunities for fraud and kickbacks.

matters.title: Asset research for WA proceedings
matters.text: Identifying land, company interests, tenements and other assets held in Western Australia by a judgment or award debtor, using state title searches, ASIC records and litigation history, to support counsel considering freezing orders or enforcement in the Supreme Court of Western Australia or the Federal Court.

local_context.title: WA investigator licensing
local_context.text: In Western Australia, anyone acting as an investigator for reward must be licensed under the Security and Related Activities (Control) Act 1996 and its 1997 regulations, administered by WA Police Licensing Services. Investigators need a Certificate III in Investigative Services and must be fit and proper persons, and they may work only for a licensed inquiry agent. Licensed work includes investigating conduct and character, related surveillance and missing persons inquiries.

local_context.title: Courts sitting in Perth
local_context.text: The Supreme Court of Western Australia sits in Perth and hears major commercial disputes, with a dedicated list for commercial and managed cases, and the Court of Appeal hears appeals. The Federal Court of Australia has a Perth registry for corporations, insolvency and federal matters. Both courts can grant freezing orders where there is a real risk of dissipation, and both support arbitration through enforcement of awards.

local_context.title: Surveillance and evidence rules
local_context.text: Western Australia has its own Surveillance Devices Act 1998, which restricts the use of listening, optical and tracking devices and the publication of recordings. Its rules differ in detail from those of other states, so methods that are lawful in Sydney or Melbourne cannot be assumed lawful in Perth. Evidence obtained improperly may be challenged in WA proceedings, which makes planning of any fieldwork with WA lawyers essential.

local_context.title: Titles, tenements and company records
local_context.text: Land in Western Australia is recorded on the Torrens register maintained by Landgate, and title searches show registered proprietors and registered interests. Mining tenements are recorded in the state's online mineral titles system, which shows holders, status and dealings. Company information comes from ASIC's national register, and ASX announcements are a key source for the many listed explorers based in Perth.

local_context.title: WA integrity and regulatory bodies
local_context.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission of Western Australia is based in Perth and publishes reports on misconduct in the state public sector, which are useful in procurement and government-facing reviews. State regulators for mines, petroleum, safety and environment publish compliance and enforcement information, and ASIC and the ASX maintain Perth offices that oversee the city's large population of listed companies.

tdsc_approach: TDSC handles Perth matters from Nashville and has no office or licence in Australia. Engagements begin by identifying the records that apply: ASIC and ASX filings, Landgate title searches, mineral tenement records, Supreme Court and Federal Court files, insolvency notices and regulator reports. Where interviews, attendance at addresses or observation are needed, TDSC coordinates investigators licensed in Western Australia under the Security and Related Activities (Control) Act 1996 and agrees methods with the client's Australian lawyers so that the Surveillance Devices Act 1998 (WA) and evidence rules are respected. Personal information is handled with the Privacy Act 1988 in mind.

faqs.q: Does an investigator working in Perth need a WA licence?
faqs.a: Yes. Acting as an investigator for reward in Western Australia requires a licence under the Security and Related Activities (Control) Act 1996, issued through WA Police Licensing Services, and investigators must work for a licensed inquiry agent. Licences from other states do not automatically apply, though temporary licences are available. TDSC coordinates appropriately licensed WA investigators where fieldwork is needed.

faqs.q: How can we verify a Perth explorer's tenement claims?
faqs.a: Western Australia's mineral titles records show the registered holder, status and dealings for each tenement. These are compared with ASX announcements, ASIC records and any joint venture or farm-in disclosures. Discrepancies, pending objections or tenements held by related parties are reported so the client can raise them with the company and its advisers.

faqs.q: Why are so many ASX-listed companies based in Perth?
faqs.a: Perth is the headquarters city of the Western Australian resources industry, and the City of Perth reports 683 ASX-listed companies based in the state, about a third of the market. Many are exploration and development companies whose value rests on tenements, drilling results and management credibility, which is why director and promoter diligence matters.

faqs.q: Which court hears a major commercial dispute in Perth?
faqs.a: Usually the Supreme Court of Western Australia, which manages complex commercial cases in a dedicated list, or the Federal Court of Australia's Perth registry where federal law, corporations or insolvency issues are engaged. The choice is for counsel. TDSC supports either with background research and asset identification ahead of freezing or enforcement applications.

faqs.q: Are WA surveillance rules the same as in other Australian states?
faqs.a: No. Western Australia has its own Surveillance Devices Act 1998, and its rules on listening, optical and tracking devices and on publishing recordings differ in detail from other states. Any surveillance connected to a Perth matter is planned with WA lawyers and carried out only by licensed WA investigators within those rules.
